html:
The siege of Masada was the last act of the first Jewish revolt against Rome. In about 73 or 74 CE a Roman legion took Masada, a fortress on a cliff-top plateau above the Dead Sea, held by Jewish rebels, the Sicarii.

The rebels had held it since the start of the revolt, after the destruction of the Temple in 70. The Romans under Flavius Silva built a ring of camps and a huge earth ramp up the western side, still visible today. According to the historian Josephus, when the wall was breached the 960 defenders killed themselves rather than be enslaved.

Excavated in the 1960s, Masada became a symbol of resistance for modern Israel. It was first fortified by Herod the Great and is a World Heritage Site.
